profile.reading: This registry row was originally tagged Digital Realty New York HVN10 and mapped to Trumbull, Connecticut, but Digital Realty's current New York and New Jersey regional facility listings no longer include an HVN10 code or any Connecticut area facility. A Data Center Dynamics article confirms Digital Realty listed this data center, outside New Haven, Connecticut, for sale, and independent aggregator listings, DatacenterMap among them, now show the building under a new operator, Aphorio Carter, a data center company descended from Carter Validus, at 15 megawatts of capacity. This registry's operator field has been corrected to Aphorio Carter accordingly, with Digital Realty retained as former_operator per this registry's no deletion policy. The building sits at 80 Merritt Boulevard, Trumbull, Connecticut 06611. No operator confirmed square footage, year built, or further facility specific detail beyond the 15 megawatt aggregator figure was located this session; Aphorio Carter's own site was not successfully reached for a dedicated facility page, and this registry's WebSearch access was unavailable at the time of the original correction. Aphorio Carter and its predecessor Carter Validus have historically focused on acquiring and operating data center and other specialized real estate assets as an institutional investor, a model similar to GI Partners and other landlord style data center owners already on file elsewhere in this registry, rather than marketing colocation directly under a well known retail brand. Aphorio Carter, a subsidiary of Carter Funds focused on mission-critical infrastructure and data center real estate, acquired the Trumbull property from Digital Realty for 10 million dollars in December 2024 after it had been listed for sale that October. The 8.26 acre site houses two data center pods and a disaster recovery pod totaling 227,500 square feet, with 15MW of utility power, in a building originally constructed in 1960. The Trumbull deal was Carter Funds seventh critical infrastructure acquisition in two years, following purchases in Bryan, Texas, Tucson, Arizona, Collierville, Tennessee, and Denver, Colorado, as the firm builds a national data center real estate portfolio it describes as spanning 125 facilities globally. Anchor tenants at the time of acquisition included a global financial services group, a FINRA-registered broker-dealer, and an automated equities trading firm, reflecting Fairfield Countys role as a low-latency corridor for New York area financial firms.

reading.body:
Aphorio Carter operates HVN10, a 15 megawatt data center campus in Trumbull, Connecticut, acquired from Digital Realty in December 2024. The facility occupies 227,500 square feet across two data center pods and a disaster recovery pod on an 8.26 acre site originally built in 1960. At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, 15 megawatts of IT load is roughly 375 racks.

HVN10 ranks third by published capacity among the five mapped data center facilities in Connecticut, and represents nearly two-thirds of the state's total published megawatt capacity of 8 megawatts. Connecticut publishes capacity figures for only two of its five mapped facilities. Aphorio Carter has deployed this facility as part of a national portfolio spanning 125 facilities globally, with seven acquisitions in two years focused on mission-critical infrastructure real estate.

At acquisition, HVN10 housed anchor tenants in financial services, including a FINRA-registered broker-dealer and an automated equities trading firm, positioning the site within Fairfield County's low-latency corridor serving New York area financial markets. No operator publications were found regarding current tenants, colocation terms, available capacity, or grid characteristics beyond the 15 megawatt utility power allocation.
